newsitem.title: USA: Xeta Q1 hit by lower phone equipment sales.
newsitem.headline: Xeta Q1 hit by lower phone equipment sales.

text.p: Xeta Corp said on Tuesday that lower telephone equipment revenue hurt its January 31 first-quarter results, but the situation is improving.
"This shortfall in PBX sales was compounded as installation of several PBX systems were delayed until the second quarter at the customers' requests," said president John Ingram in a statement.

Ingram said phone equipment orders rose sharply during the quarter, and Xeta entered the second quarter with "a backlog of over $2 million in PBX orders which is about 500 percent of our normal backlog level."
He said most of the backlog is scheduled for second quarter installation, "which will put us back on track to record our fourth consecutive record year."
For the first quarter, Xeta reported earnings of $0.14 a share, down from $0.19 a year ago. Sales fell to $2.9 million from $3.6 million.
